subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Lin <katie@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Hi Katie — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps so we stay aligned:

Key requirements (as discussed)
- Data: PII and customer IDs must remain in Acme VPC; logging/audit retention required (SOC2).
- Performance: steady-state ~50 req/s, expected short peaks up to ~120 req/s for ~10 minutes.
- Payload: avg prompt ~250 tokens, avg completion ~500 tokens (total ~750 tokens per request).
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 preferable, 500ms p95 acceptable for most routes.
- Security/compliance: need Private VPC option or dedicated tenancy; must support KMS.

High-level deployment modes to consider
1) Hosted API: fastest to launch, per-token billing, Redwood managed; good for quick experiments and when strict VPC isolation is not required.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and isolation, monthly reserved commit + burst; good if you want steady capacity with an SLA.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation and control, longer lead time and higher fixed costs.

Next steps
- I'll put together a short cost model comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private using the traffic assumptions above and include committed capacity recommendations. (attached: deployment_assumptions.xlsx)
- Can you confirm the peak pattern (120 req/s for ~10 minutes) is the worst-case burst and whether both read/write routes need same SLOs?
- Suggest a 30-min follow-up next week to review numbers and tradeoffs.

Thanks — cc'ing Aditya for any technical clarifications.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications: 
- Confirming the steady-state is ~50 req/s across our API. We see spikes up to ~120 req/s but only for short windows (typically <15 minutes).
- Token counts you used are correct on avg (250 prompt / 500 completion). Heavy prompts can reach ~2k tokens but those are <1% of traffic.
- Priority: data isolation (VPC) > latency > cost. If we can get VPC + predictable latency, we can justify higher fixed cost.

I've attached our RFP questions and a CSV with a week of traffic to show peaks. Also: can you include a hosted-fallback scenario where critical routes use Dedicated/Private and non-sensitive calls fall back to Hosted API?

Available next Tue/Thu morning PST for the follow-up.

Appreciate the clarifications, Katie — based on your priority (VPC > latency > cost) and the traffic pattern you shared, attached is a first-pass cost comparison and recommended starting configuration. High-level summary below; details in redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx.

1) Hosted API (per-token) — pros: no infra/setup; cons: not VPC-first
- Estimated monthly usage: 50 req/s steady-state (~3.24M requests/month) * 750 tokens/request = ~2.4B tokens/month
- Example rate (hosted): $0.0012 / 1K output tokens + $0.0004 / 1K input tokens (model-dependent)
- Monthly estimate (hosted only): ~$5,800 — note this is variable and scales with usage; good for pilot or mixed-mode fallback.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — pros: isolation, predictable latency; cons: commit required
- Starting recommendation: 4x A100-equivalent workers reserved to meet steady-state with headroom for short bursts via burst pool.
- Monthly reserved commit estimate: ~$12,000/month (capacity-based fee) + per-request marginal cost lower than hosted.
- For your peak windows, we recommend burst capacity policy rather than large overcommit.

3) Private VPC / On-prem — pros: full isolation & compliance; cons: setup time and higher fixed cost
- One-time setup + integration: ~$65,000 (includes private control plane, PKI/KMS integration, and initial deployment engineering)
- Ongoing platform fee + infra: ~$18,000/month (depends on cloud infra choices)

Mixed recommendation (based on priorities)
- Primary: Dedicated reserved in your VPC (or dedicated tenancy) to meet latency and isolation needs.
- Fallback: Hosted API for non-sensitive/low-priority routes to reduce required reserved commit and monthly cost.

Open questions for the follow-up call
- Which routes must be strictly VPC-only (auth, data in, logging)?
- Do you want dedicated KV/cache for embeddings or shared cache?
- How comfortable is procurement with a one-time setup vs capitalizing it?

Can we schedule Thu 10:00am PST to walk through the pricing sheet and I'll have Aditya and Dev on for technical questions.

Thanks,
Marissa
